description: The pie chart represents the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset. The chart is divided into six slices, each representing a different emotion category. The slices are labeled as Frustration (light blue, 25.1%), Neutral (blue, 23.1%), Anger (yellow, 14.9%), Sadness (orange, 14.7%), Excitement (red, 14.1%), and Happiness (dark red, 8.1%). The percentages are displayed inside each slice. The chart does not include a legend, and the slices are not visually emphasized. The slices are arranged in a clockwise order, with the largest slice, Frustration, positioned at the top left, followed by Neutral, and the remaining slices in a particular order, with the smallest slice, Happiness, at the bottom right.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages displayed relative to the number of utterances. Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger and Sadness are nearly equal, with Anger slightly higher at 15.9% and Sadness at 14.7%. Excitement and Happiness are the smallest categories, with Happiness at 10.1% and Excitement at 14.1%. Notably, the data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions (Excitement and Happiness) compared to negative ones (Frustration, Anger, and Sadness). The chart provides a clear visual representation of the emotional distribution, with labels positioned outside each slice for clarity.
